message.content:
Review: The experiment is clearly organized around two distinct questions: whether the controls reproducibly affect polarization as intended, and whether calibrated control improves a computing task. The sequence from source verification and instrument calibration through randomized measurements, prespecified criteria, analysis, and task comparison is understandable. It also appropriately treats the supplied scans as motivation rather than independent evidence, preserves their different DOP scales, and limits conclusions to the original apparatus.

Feedback: Several choices remain open, so the design is not yet fully reproducible. Specify how the pilot will select the grid and its resolution, how the polarimeter’s calibration and validation states will be divided, and how the validation tolerance will be set if instrument specifications and residual-based criteria differ. Define the target-control mapping and low-to-high contrasts explicitly, or state how they will be selected if source verification does not support the proposed mapping. Give a concrete method for setting the practical effect and equivalence bounds, including the planned power target and how pilot uncertainty will affect run count. For the computing comparison, clarify what “calibrated controls” and the baseline configuration mean operationally, and how paired trials will be analyzed. Finally, “distinguishable from zero” for DOP and “relevant environmental or alignment changes” need prespecified statistical or recording criteria. These are mostly implementation details, but they matter to interpreting and reproducing the results.

Rating (1-5): 4
